editor.short_hint: Leave out amounts already included in your current cash flow.
editor.plan_hint: Add the details that matter to you. You can skip any stage.
editor.age_error: Use whole ages: current 18–75, retirement later and no more than 80, end later than retirement and no more than 120.
editor.assets_hint: Available assets fund cash flow. Property and other non-liquid assets only contribute to net worth.
editor.skip_disabled: Remove the recorded amounts before skipping this stage.
editor.partner_hint: Record only a partner's contribution to your plan or additional costs. Do not repeat amounts already included in your personal cash flow.
editor.split_hint: These amounts are part of your working-life spending total. Classification alone does not add costs; a larger total requires confirmation.
editor.additional_hint: Add items not already in your monthly totals. They are counted separately for the dates you enter.
editor.name: Item name
editor.event_error: Check the name, amount and dates: use a positive amount, an end no earlier than the start, and dates within the plan.
editor.yearly_hint: This yearly record is kept as imported; edit it through a backup for now.

flow.discard: You have changes that have not been applied. Leave and discard them?
flow.trust: In today's money · Not a guaranteed return

hints.assets: Start from your baseline. Update only what has changed.
hints.career: Plan different periods of work and income.
hints.partner: What will your partner contribute, or what extra costs will you cover?
hints.child: Allow for the periods when you will support a child.
hints.housing: Add cash costs for renting, buying, or other housing needs.
hints.parents: Set aside the support you expect to provide for your parents.
hints.retirement: How much will you need to pay yourself each month after retiring?
hints.events: Add travel, education, or another life event.
hints.advanced: Amounts are in today's money. Adjust the assumptions behind the estimate.

career.error: Check amounts and dates. Job periods must not overlap each other, nor may break periods. Both must end by retirement. A break may occur within a job. Existing income breakdowns must be fully classified.

hints.salary: Replaces your salary during these months. Your original income path resumes afterward.
hints.side_income: Enter net income not already in your baseline, with its own start and end dates.
hints.break: Salary is zero during these months. Existing side income continues; your original salary path resumes afterward.

career.growth_hint: Set annual growth for your current salary. Enter a new salary separately when changing jobs.
career.growth_detail: Real growth is the change in purchasing power after inflation, not the nominal pay rise. 0% preserves purchasing power. The annual rate is compounded monthly; it does not imply monthly pay reviews. This affects the current salary baseline only. Existing new-job and side-income periods retain their own growth rates. Presets are input shortcuts, not forecasts.
career.growth_error: Enter an annual real growth rate between -99% and 100%.

charts.peak: Spending peaks in {year}, at {amount} for the year.
charts.balance_hint: See how long your available funds last. Net worth also includes non-cash assets and deducts debt.
charts.minimum: Lowest monthly available funds: {amount} in {year}. Lines show year-end balances.
charts.same_balances: Net worth matches available funds; one line is shown
charts.negative_hint: Below zero indicates a cash shortfall

analysis.title: What your plan shows
analysis.basis: Calculated from your inputs and fixed rules. No AI.
analysis.actions_hint: Compare before applying. These are scenarios to explore, not life advice.
analysis.cause_verified: Controlled check: removing this housing payment delays or removes the first shortfall.

housing-causes-first-gap.title: Housing costs are close to the first shortfall
housing-causes-first-gap.body: The first shortfall occurs within 12 months of a one-off housing payment. You can test a different date.

housing-child-overlap.title: Housing and child costs start close together
housing-child-overlap.body: These arrangements start within 24 months of each other. More cash may be needed during this period.

liquidity-gap.title: Positive net worth does not guarantee available cash
liquidity-gap.body: Some months have negative available funds despite positive net worth. Non-cash assets are not automatically spent.

retirement-transition-gap.title: A shortfall appears early in retirement
retirement-transition-gap.body: The first shortfall is in the first retirement year, without retirement income already active. Review self-funded spending.

retirement-spend-sensitive.title: Retirement spending strongly affects the endpoint
retirement-spend-sensitive.body: A 10% increase in retirement spending ranks among the three largest endpoint impacts. Compare different budgets.

zero-return-conservative.title: No real return on available funds is assumed
zero-return-conservative.body: At least 120 months have positive balances while the real return is 0%. Review the assumption without treating positive returns as guaranteed.

important-total-unclassified.title: Some expenses are still estimated as a total
important-total-unclassified.body: Totals work for planning. To understand individual categories, split existing totals rather than adding the same costs again.

baseline-sustainable.title: No shortfall under the included arrangements
baseline-sustainable.body: Each stage is filled in or explicitly excluded. This is a scenario based on current inputs, not a guarantee.

delay-housing.title: Change housing payment timing
delay-housing.tradeoff: Only the cash payment date changes. House prices, loans, rent, and child arrangements are not adjusted automatically.

retirement-budget.title: Compare self-funded retirement budgets
retirement-budget.tradeoff: Lower spending means a different retirement budget. Healthcare and care needs do not automatically decrease.

retire-later.title: Compare retirement dates
retire-later.tradeoff: The baseline work-income and retirement-spending boundary changes. Independently scheduled work, pensions, and events keep their own dates.

opening-cash.title: Review opening available assets
opening-cash.tradeoff: Use only existing accessible funds, not expected future earnings or property valuations.

simulation.description: Changes are made to a copy, not your saved plan.
simulation.stale: Your plan has changed. This comparison is out of date; close and reopen it.
simulation.error: This change cannot be calculated. Check amounts, dates, and conflicts with existing periods.
simulation.exclusions: Unentered expenses, policy changes, and uncertain future events are excluded. Returns are not guaranteed.

evidence.title: Calculation basis
evidence.description: Review inputs, assumptions, and monthly calculation records.
evidence.basis: Today's purchasing power. Growth and returns are real rates; inflation is not added again. Non-cash assets do not automatically cover cash shortfalls.
evidence.no_records: No separate records for this month.
